method: Each note is read as a letter from A to G, up to two sharps or flats (ASCII b and # plus the musical signs), and an optional octave from -1 to 9 that defaults to 4; a mixed accidental such as b# and any other malformed note is refused, and at most one reply names the field's accepted form. The interval number comes from the number of letter names spanned, counted inclusive, so C to E is a third even when the notes are written C flat to E sharp. The quality compares the actual semitone count with the major or perfect size of that number, one octave up from a simple interval when the letters cross octaves: no difference is perfect or major, one semitone less is diminished or minor, one more is augmented, and further double accidentals give doubly, triply, quintuply and sextuply forms. The result names the interval, its simple form and octave count, the inversion (number complemented to nine with major and minor swapped and augmented and diminished swapped), the cents as 100 per semitone and the frequency ratio as 2^(semitones/12) in 12-tone equal temperament. The name always follows the written letters, so C sharp to F is a diminished fourth while D flat to F, the same four semitones, is a major third. Intervals larger than a fifteenth are worded as a simple interval plus a number of octaves. The page does not model just intonation, key signatures, microtonal temperaments or sounding pitch of transposing instruments, and it runs entirely in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: An interval's number counts the letter names from the lower note to the upper one inclusive, so C to E is a third and C to A is a sixth regardless of accidentals.

A major second is two semitones, a major third four, a perfect fourth five, a perfect fifth seven, a major sixth nine, a major seventh eleven and an octave twelve; altered intervals are named from how far they sit above or below these sizes.

Inversion complements an interval's number to nine and swaps major with minor and augmented with diminished, so a major third inverts to a minor sixth; in 12-tone equal temperament an interval of n semitones spans 100n cents and a frequency ratio of 2^(n/12).
